opts.title: MAX/MIN macros use FastMax/FastMin (return by value) instead of std::max/std::min (return by const reference)
opts.source: NQM_FAST_COMP (Delnar; randomascii.wordpress.com 'std::min causing three times slowdown on VC')
opts.hotspot: every MAX/MIN use (A*, danger plots, cities, units, voting ...) and the NQM_FAST_COMP blocks in CvGameCoreUtils.h, CvCity, CvFractal, CvMap, CvPlot, CvPreGame, CvWorldBuilderMapLoader
opts.gain: not measured; expected small, spread over the whole DLL
opts.iteration_order: No loop touched. FastMax/FastMin evaluate the same comparison as VC2008 std::max/std::min (_DEBUG_LT(a, b) ? b : a and _DEBUG_LT(b, a) ? b : a), so the same operand is chosen, ties included.
opts.rng: Both forms are function templates taking const T&, so every argument is evaluated exactly once in both; RNG calls inside MAX/MIN arguments (if any) keep their count and order.
opts.float: For float/double the chosen operand is an object of type T already in memory (const T& parameter; temporaries are rounded to T in both versions), so returning it by value instead of by reference cannot change its value. Class A4 only because of the spec's float rule: the macro also expands in functions with float code, so the fpu_cw axis runs on standard.
opts.equivalence: detlab equiv standard + fpu_cw axis (53/24/64 bit).
files: existing NQM_FAST_COMP blocks in CvGameCoreUtils.h, CvCity.cpp, CvFractal.cpp, CvMap.cpp, CvPlot.cpp, CvPreGame.cpp, CvWorldBuilderMapLoader.cpp
opts.notes: Changes code generation wherever MAX/MIN is used (about 250 sites, many inside dormant AUI blocks).

opts.title: CvPreGame::GetGameOption(const char*): memo of the by-name lookup (custom options scan + SQL default fallback) with exact invalidation
opts.source: hand-written (profile-baseline ranking item 1)
opts.hotspot: CvGame::isOption(const char*) -> CvPreGame::GetGameOption(const char*): SQL fallback 'Select "Default" from GameOptions' 51-58% of Update with empty game_options, linear strncmp scan over s_GameOptions 10% with all options set (callers: CvCity::IsCanPurchase/canConstruct, CvCitySiteEvaluator::CanFound, CvWonderProductionAI::ChooseWonder, 152 call sites)
opts.gain: x2.58 (95% CI 2.50-2.67) with empty game_options (pangaea6 x2.60, stress-large10 x2.56); x1.12 (95% CI 1.07-1.17) with all options set (only the strncmp scan goes: pangaea6 x1.08, stress-large10 x1.16)
opts.iteration_order: The memoised value is produced by the unchanged golden body (GetGameOptionUncached: same s_GameOptions scan order, same strncmp prefix rule, first match wins, then the same SELECT); the memo only returns it again. No caller loop changes. The memo is keyed by the bytes of the name (FNV-1a + memcmp of the whole name), never by pointer, and its slot layout does not influence any result.
opts.rng: No RNG in GetGameOption or anywhere on its path (vector scan, sqlite SELECT). Callers are unchanged, so their RNG calls keep count and order.
opts.float: No floating point involved (string compare, int result).
opts.equivalence: Result = f(s_GameOptions, game database, name); f reads nothing else and writes nothing (read-only SELECT). Invalidation: every write of s_GameOptions (SetGameOption x2, SetGameOptions, read/readArchive, ResetGameOptions) is followed by SyncGameOptionsWithEnumList(), which now invalidates first (s_GameOptions is file-local to CvPreGame.cpp and no other writer exists; s_preGameArchive has no delta/sync users). The database can change only on (re)load: CvDllDatabaseUtility::PerformDatabasePostProcessing (end), CacheGameDatabaseData (start and end, also covers LEKMOD post-DLC loading), FlushGameDatabaseData and CvGlobals::SetGameDatabase invalidate. Mod Lua only SELECTs from the DB. iValue is written only when found, as in golden. Names of 64+ bytes bypass the memo.
opts.shadow: Every memo hit runs the golden lookup again (GameOptionMemoMatches) and reports OnOptVerifyMismatch(10, "CvPreGame::GetGameOption memo") / exit 86 on any difference in found flag or value.
files: LEKMOD_DLL/CvGameCoreDLL_Expansion2/CvPreGame.cpp (memo, GetGameOptionUncached = golden body, invalidation in SyncGameOptionsWithEnumList; golden GetGameOption body kept in #else)
opts.notes: Helps the real game as well: the DLL asks for hidden options and code-only options (GAMEOPTION_AI_TWEAKS, ...) that a setup screen never writes into s_GameOptions, so the SQL fallback runs in real games too (the 37-visible-options scenario still spends 35% of Update in it). Removes ~all sqlite and most det-heap allocation traffic from the turn. GetGameOption(GameOptionTypes) with an out-of-range hash and GetMapOption(const char*) are not memoised (not hot).

opts.title: CvUnit::setXY/setDamage bully-icon block: the (major x minor) CanMajorBullyGold table with one military ranking per table and one local-power scan per minor
opts.source: hand-written (profile-baseline ranking item 2; works in the real game too, not a headless-only shortcut)
opts.hotspot: UPDATE_MINOR_BG_ICON_ON_UNIT_MOVE_OR_SET_DAMAGE (CvUnit::setXY, CvUnit::setDamage) -> CvMinorCivAI::CanMajorBullyGold -> CalculateBullyMetric: 7% (pangaea6), 15% (Large), 24% (Huge) of Update with options set
opts.gain: x1.13 (95% CI 1.03-1.23) on options-set scenarios: pangaea6 (6 civs) x1.055, stress-large10 (10 civs + 20 CS) x1.21; the profile share of the block drops from 15% to ~3.5% on Large
opts.iteration_order: The decision loop after the move is golden's (minor outer, major inner, same alive checks, same updateFog call and break), so the UI side effect (updateFog -> GameplayFOWChanged) hits the same plots in the same order; only the values it compares come from a table built just before the loop instead of lazily inside it. Inside the table: the military ranking is the same CvWeightedVector push/SortItems sequence as golden, built once per table instead of once per pair (its input does not change within a block); the local power scan visits the same plots and units in the same order and sums per owner (integer sums do not depend on order).
opts.rng: No RNG in CanMajorBullyGold / CalculateBullyMetric (bForUnit=false, no tooltip) or in the table code. The only state write on the path is CvPlayer::GetMilitaryMight's lazy per-turn refresh (m_iTurnMightRecomputed, m_iMilitaryMight, m_iEconomicMight): the table calls GetMilitaryMight for the same players, in the same order, at the same point and under the same condition as golden's first CalculateBullyMetric call of the block (some alive major and some alive minor slot), so the refresh happens at the identical moment.
opts.float: The two float expressions of CalculateBullyMetric are copied verbatim with identical integer inputs: fRankRatio = (float)(size - iRanking) / (float)size -> (int)(fRankRatio * 50) and fLocalPowerRatio = (float)iBully / (float)iMinor compared with the same double literals. No reordering, no float<->double change, no new intermediate variable (both were float locals in golden and stay float locals). Class A4 because of the float rule: needs the fpu_cw axis.
opts.equivalence: detlab equiv starter + realistic (both equal) and shadow (every table entry compared with golden CanMajorBullyGold) on as-is and options-set scenarios incl. the Large stress map with 20 city-states. opts.rng: Exactly one getAsyncRandNum(count, "Diplomacy Rand") call with the same count, only when the count is positive, as in golden; no synchronous RNG involved. The chosen text reaches synced state through CvNotifications (player segments), so the realistic equivalence runs check the pick.

Memo lifetime = golden's prepared m_pDiploResponseQuery: cleared in CvGame::uninit (reset on new game and load), plus a database epoch (bumped in CvGlobals::SetGameDatabase and in the database utility's post-processing/cache/flush entry points) drops it if the database is reloaded while the game object lives. NULL leader/response bypass the memo (golden behaviour).
opts.shadow: Every memo hit re-runs the golden query and compares the row list (OnOptVerifyMismatch(16, "CvGame::GetDiploResponse memo") / exit 86).

opts.title: CvGameTrade::IsValidTradeRoutePath / CvTradeAI::GetAvailableTR: memo of the international trade-route A* result (found, cost, path) across calls and turns, invalidated per map block of the plots the search read
opts.source: hand-written (agent-C profile, turns 151-200 stress-large10-s31-opts-all: IsValidTradeRoutePath 9.3% of Update, of which GetNumPotentialConnections from the (No)NeedInternationalTradeRoute city strategies 7.4% and GetAvailableTR 1.8%; the two trade-route finders do 55% of all A* steps)
opts.hotspot: CvCityStrategyAI::DoTurn -> IsTestCityStrategy_(No)NeedInternationalTradeRoute -> CvPlayerTrade::GetNumPotentialConnections -> CvGameTrade::IsValidTradeRoutePath; CvHomelandAI::ExecuteTradeUnitMoves -> CvTradeAI::PrioritizeTradeRoutes -> GetAvailableTR (CvAStar::GeneratePath with the TradeRouteLand/Water callbacks)
opts.gain: x1.052, 95% CI [1.030, 1.074] over c-optset (20 paired rounds, turns 151-200 from the turn-150 checkpoints): stress-large10-s31-opts-all x1.051 (paired median; min-sum 1.054), stress-large10-s31 x1.072 (1.047; mean 1.069 [1.045, 1.094]), pangaea6-opts-all x1.060 (1.093), pangaea6 x1.052 (1.052); vs golden-hyg the optset goes 1.95 -> 2.04, 3.87 -> 4.06, 1.72 -> 1.82, 3.20 -> 3.35 (paired medians)
opts.iteration_order: No loop is touched: GetNumPotentialConnections, GetAvailableTR and every other caller iterate as before; IsValidTradeRoutePath returns the bool golden computes from the same (found, last node m_iTotalCost) and the same fresh GetTradeRouteRange, after the same isCoastal tests; GetAvailableTR pushes the same plot list in the same order (the last node's parent chain, origin first, exactly as CopyPathIntoTradeConnection). A search is skipped only when its outcome is provably the stored one: every trade-route search uses bReuse = false (starts from cleared nodes), so it is a function of the key (origin and destination plot index, origin player, team, canEmbarkAllWaterPassage, RiverTradeRoad and MoveFriendlyWoodsAsRoad traits, and for water the origin team's war bit set) and of the plot inputs its callbacks read; the four callbacks record the map block (at most 16 x 16 blocks) of both plots they read, and an entry is used only while its domain epoch is unchanged and no recorded block was stamped after it was stored. The table (2-way set associative, FNV-1a over the key contents, least-recently-used replacement) decides only which searches run, never a result.
opts.rng: No RNG: TradePathInitialize, TradeRouteHeuristic, PathDest, TradeRouteLand/WaterValid and PathCost, isCoastal and GetTradeRouteRange are pure reads (no getJonRandNum/getMapRandNum, no Lua hook on this path). The memo is not game state and is never serialised.
opts.float: No floating point (integer path costs and ranges).
opts.equivalence: detlab equiv c-golden-hyg (current hyg set) vs c-o22b: starter 3/3, realistic 12/12; shadow c-o22b-sh: starter 3/3, realistic 12/12, stress-large10-s31-opts-all + stress-huge12-s41-opts-all 200 turns 2/2, plus three runs from late checkpoints (stress-large10-s31 and -opts-all turns 151-200, pangaea6-opts-all turns 101-200), no mismatch; pairbench digests equal on turns 151-200 of all four late scenarios (c-golden-hyg, c-optset2, c-o22b). Invalidation: the trade-path plot inputs are written only by CvPlot setters (reset, setArea, setOwner, setPlotType incl. its isAdjacentToLand writes, setTerrainType, setFeatureType, setRouteType, changeRiverCrossingCount, setPlotCity, updateImpassable), CvPlot::read (followed by CvMap::setup), CvMap::updateAdjacency, CvPlayer::addCity/deleteCity (isCity needs the city object) and CvPlayer::setTeam (getTeam of the player's plots); each bumps right after its write: route presence, feature (land) and the owner of a water plot (water) stamp the block of their plot, all other (rare) writers void the whole domain.
opts.shadow: optimized-diag: every memo hit also runs the golden search and compares found, m_iTotalCost and the full parent chain node by node (HEADLESS_OPT_VERIFY id 22); the diag build therefore runs golden's search sequence.

opts.iteration_order: Golden's loops add entry->Get(key) for every entry in ascending id order; the new loops visit, in the same ascending order, only the entries whose getter can return nonzero for the key (relevance = the getter itself evaluated over every flag combination at build time) and apply golden's per-entry tests unchanged (m_pabHasPolicy, IsPolicyBlocked, GetNumBuilding > 0, entry != NULL). Skipped entries add 0 in golden; integer sums. Keys outside the built range run golden's loop. The city loop of the landmass block is unchanged and skipped entirely when no building has a landmass yield for the yield.
opts.rng: No RNG: entry getters, HasPolicy/IsPolicyBlocked, GetNumBuilding and getBuildingInfo are const reads.
opts.equivalence: The lists are a pure function of the loaded database entries (CvPolicyEntry / CvBuildingEntry arrays are filled by PrefetchCollection and never written during a game). Rebuilt when g_uiHeadlessDbStaticEpoch moves - bumped in CvGlobals::SetGameDatabase, CvGlobals::infoTypeFromStringReset and at the four OPT-0016 database sites (CacheGameDatabaseData start/end, FlushGameDatabaseData, PerformDatabasePostProcessing) - or when the entry/key count differs. opts.float: The double expressions of IsYieldDeficient (GetYieldAverage ratio, citystrategyround(x * 100)) stay textually unchanged in the same function; only their bool result is reused within the scope, under the same x87 control word.
opts.equivalence: IsYieldDeficient(e) reads the owner's plot list, which plots the city works, calculateYield of those plots (const reads) and a define. Inside the scopes nothing writes that state; the only foreign code is CanBuyPlot's CityCanBuyPlot GameEvents hook: LuaSupport::Call* now moves g_uiHeadlessLuaListenerEpoch after every hook call that had listeners and the memo clears on a moved epoch; inside a nested hook call (a listener calling back into the DLL) the memo is bypassed (g_iHeadlessLuaHookDepth).
opts.shadow: optimized-diag: every memo hit recomputes golden's value and compares (HEADLESS_OPT_VERIFY id 42).

opts.gain: leave-one-out in the full set, with agent C's OPT-0022 trade-path memo present (r6, 6 rounds): x1.019 (95% CI 1.018-1.020); Large opts-all 1.018, pangaea6 opts-all 1.012, Large as-is 1.024, pangaea6 as-is 1.021 [headless/out/agentD/pairbench/r6-final/pairbench.json, d-f22n43 / d-f22all, 6 rounds]
opts.iteration_order: Strategy loop unchanged. Both tests are 'GetNumTradeRoutesRemaining(false) <= 0 or GetNumPotentialConnections(city, domain) <= 0' with opposite answers. Strategies 35/36 (land) and 37/38 (sea) are adjacent in the DB; the reuse is allowed only for the trigger test that directly follows the NEED test (any other trigger test clears it), and is ended when the CityStrategyCanActivate hook after the NEED test had listeners.
opts.rng: No RNG in the two tests (pure reads plus trade-route A*). The hook call stays exactly as in golden (called iff the NEED result is true).
opts.equivalence: Between the two tests only this loop's bookkeeping runs: SetUsingCityStrategy (strategy flags and adoption turn), flavour propagation into the city's own production AIs (FlavorUpdate) and logging - none of it is read by GetNumTradeRoutesRemaining / GetNumPotentialConnections (players, cities, teams, techs, beliefs, embargoes, plots, existing trade connections). Pathfinder state: the trade-route finders are only ever run with bReuse = false (all 6 GeneratePath sites) and every GetLastNode read follows its own GeneratePath, so skipping the repeated searches leaves the finder in the state of its last search, which is the same search in both orders; their callbacks (TradePathInitialize, TradeRoute*Valid/PathCost) write only the finder's scratch buffer.
opts.shadow: optimized-diag: every reuse also runs golden's NO_NEED test and compares (HEADLESS_OPT_VERIFY id 43); the diag build therefore follows golden's search sequence.

A class is left out only if its term is 0 for every city of that civilization: no class info, no civilization building, no building entry, or (per loop) no belief with BuildingClassTourism != 0 / MountainTourism <= 0 / TechEnhancedTourism <= 0 (times a positive count stays <= 0) / no policy with BuildingClassTourismModifier != 0.
opts.rng: No RNG: the terms are const reads (GetNumBuilding, belief/policy sums, HasTech).
opts.float: No floating point involved (integer sums; the later percentage multiply is unchanged).
opts.equivalence: Skipped terms are pure reads that evaluate to 0, so the integer sums are identical. The lists depend only on the loaded database (civilization buildings, building, belief and policy entries) and are rebuilt with OPT-0041's DB epoch or a count change; an out-of-range or missing civilization falls back to golden's loop.
opts.shadow: optimized-diag: every sum is recomputed over all building classes with the same per-class code and compared (HEADLESS_OPT_VERIFY id 49).

opts.title: CvAStar open list: an index of the sorted list as runs of equal cost (cost buckets) finds the insertion place by binary search instead of walking the linked list; the list itself, its order and every pointer write stay golden's
opts.source: hand-written (AI CPU plan of the civ5-reimagened server, 3.1 a: CvAStar::AddToOpen was 17 % self time of the AI phase of game 936, turns 126-127)
opts.hotspot: CvAStar::AddToOpen (O(n) walk from the head or the tail of a sorted doubly linked list) and the walk back in CvAStar::UpdateOpenNode
opts.gain: AI phase of ring save 235 of the live game 936 (Huge, 12 majors), turns 126+127, desktop CPU, interleaved runs: 9.47-9.51 s -> 8.02-8.03 s (x1.18, -15.6 %); digests and GCS1 save hashes equal
opts.iteration_order: Golden AddToOpen (list sorted ascending by m_iTotalCost): empty list -> sole node; cost <= head cost -> new head (before its equals); cost >= tail cost -> new tail (after its equals); else if |cost - tail| < |cost - head| the walk starts at the tail and stops at the first node (from the tail) whose cost is <= the new cost, the new node goes after it; else the walk starts at the head and stops at the first node whose cost is >= the new cost, the new node goes before it. Both stops are functions of the sorted list alone: the last node with cost <= c, and the first node with cost >= c. The index keeps the list as runs of equal cost (cost, first node, last node), so these two nodes are the last node of the last run with cost <= c and the first node of the first run with cost >= c: a binary search. The branch conditions and every m_pNext / m_pPrev / m_pOpen / m_pOpenTail write, and the udNotifyList calls with their arguments (they re-enter AddToOpen through PathNodeAdd), are golden's. UpdateOpenNode: the stay-or-move test is golden's; the walk back from the predecessor ends at the last node with cost <= the new cost (the nodes behind the old place cost more than the old cost), found by the same search with the node taken out of the index first. GetBest pops the head: the first node of the lowest run. The index is rebuilt empty at the start of every new search (GeneratePath without reuse) and kept with the list when a search is reused. All changes of m_iTotalCost of an open node go through LinkChild / UpdateParents -> UpdateOpenNode (checked: no other writer), and the node carries the cost it is indexed under (m_iOpenKey).
opts.rng: None.

opts.title: TurnsToReachTarget (tactical analysis map finder): inside pure-query scopes a search stops as soon as its destination can no longer be popped, or (callers that only test <= N turns) can only be popped with more than N turns; the rest of a stopped search runs before any reuse of its tree and at the end of the scope

opts.iteration_order: Up to the stop the search makes the same Step() calls in the same order; the checks between two Step() calls only read (node list types, m_iData2 of open nodes, canMoveThrough, TA cells). The rest of a stopped search is the same Step() loop, run on the same tree and game state (inside the scope, or before a search that reuses the tree, which happens inside the same scope), so the finder leaves every scope with the golden tree. A search that does not reuse the tree does not depend on it (all listed nodes are cleared; unlisted nodes keep only cost caches, refilled per search epoch by OPT-0013; twins are fully written on entering the open list).
opts.rng: No RNG (path validity, ZOC, node data only).
